lines.line: Oia, in the bright afternoon, felt a world away.
Athens began under a grey sky, with the Acropolis still above me.
In Anafiotika’s uneven lanes, I kept looking up at the old stone wall.
At Meteora, the sandstone towers rose over the valley. Monasteries rested high on the cliffs, beneath heavy clouds.
Back in Athens, I took in the city from the top deck of a bus.
Then I finally stood on the Acropolis, beside the Caryatids, in bright sun.
On Santorini, a white Fiat 500 waited by a whitewashed building.
I drove beside the bright blue water, with pale land beyond the shore.
At Akrotiri Lighthouse, I looked up as the Greek flag moved in the wind.
I leaned toward the old viewing device, curious about the island beneath me.
By evening, the caldera islands caught the last golden light.
I settled beside the white rooftops and watched the bay grow quiet. After all that looking up, I could simply stay there a while.
